name: macOS 11 (Big Sur) or later
howToGet: Update in System Settings > General > Software Update.
howToCheck: Reads the macOS version and compares it with 11.0.

name: Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer)
howToGet: Use an M1 or newer Mac. The app is built for Apple Silicon only.
howToCheck: Not checked: an Intel Mac cannot open the app at all.

name: Loupedeck+ plugged in
howToGet: Plug the Loupedeck+ into the Mac with its USB cable, straight into the Mac if a hub drops it. Other Loupedeck models are not supported.
howToCheck: Lists the Mac's MIDI sources and looks for one called Loupedeck. Opens nothing.
without: There is nothing to press or turn. The editor still opens, but nothing reaches your apps.

name: No other app driving the same deck
howToGet: Quit the Loupedeck software and any other MIDI mapper (Bome MIDI Translator, MidiKey2Key, the old LD-RESOLVE) from their own app menu. Never force-quit them.
howToCheck: Looks for those apps among the running apps by name and bundle id. Touches nothing.
without: Both apps answer every press, so keys and clicks fire twice.

name: Accessibility permission
howToGet: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility: switch 2T5 DECK+ on. If it is already on, switch it off and on again, then restart the app.
howToCheck: Asks macOS whether this app is trusted. Never shows a prompt.
without: The deck cannot press keys, click or scroll for you.

name: Screen Recording permission
feature: Reading what is on screen: HUD placement, mouse calibration, window titles
howToGet: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording: switch 2T5 DECK+ on, then restart the app.
howToCheck: Asks macOS whether screen access is granted. Never shows a prompt.
without: Those on-screen reads come back empty. Keys, knobs and sliders still work.

name: Automation permission for Finder
howToGet: macOS asks the first time a Finder tag key is used. If you said No: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation, then allow 2T5 DECK+ to control Finder.
howToCheck: Remembers the answer from the app's first Apple Event to Finder. Until then it reads as not asked yet.
without: The Finder tag keys cannot read which files are selected.

name: macOS 15.2 or later
feature: Mouse calibration: the picture check that notices a changed Resolve layout
howToGet: Update in System Settings > General > Software Update.
howToCheck: Reads the macOS version and compares it with 15.2.
without: Calibration still works from the points you set. The automatic check that your layout has changed is off.

name: Python 3
howToGet: Install Python 3 from python.org, or with Homebrew. Nothing else to install: the Resolve helper only uses what Python ships with.
howToCheck: Looks for python3 in the usual places (Homebrew, python.org) and runs it once to read its version. Skips Apple's built-in stub when the Command Line Tools are not installed, so no install prompt appears.
without: Resolve buttons do nothing. Every other app still works.

name: DaVinci Resolve (Studio)
howToGet: Install DaVinci Resolve Studio from Blackmagic Design. Its scripting files come with it. Tested with Studio only: the free version may refuse outside scripting.
howToCheck: Looks for DaVinciResolveScript.py in Resolve's Developer/Scripting/Modules folder.
without: Resolve control is off. Every other app still works.

name: Resolve: External scripting set to Local
howToGet: Open Resolve, then DaVinci Resolve > Preferences > System > General > External scripting using: Local. Keep Resolve running.
howToCheck: Only when Resolve is running: looks at whether the helper could connect to it.
without: The deck sees Resolve but cannot talk to it, so Resolve buttons do nothing.

name: Programs your Run command keys call
feature: Keys you set to run a command
howToGet: Install whatever program the command starts. The built-in actions need nothing extra.
howToCheck: Not checked: only you know which commands you assigned.
